The (Ga,Mn)N layer is grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) at 620°C.
The substrate used for growing the (Ga,Mn)N layer is a commercially available low threading dislocation density GaN:Si template.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is 30 nm.
The junction exhibits a high resistance of over 10 MΩ at room temperature.
The ideality factor () of the Schottky junction is greater than 1.5 for T ≤ 300 K.
The Curie transition temperature of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is about 8 K.
The (Ga,Mn)N layer has a highly insulating character, rendering lateral conductivity inefficient.
The Al O layer is 100 nm thick.
The ideality factor () of the Schottky junction at 151 K is 1.7.
The ideality factor () of the Schottky junction at 300 K is 1.8.
The device is fabricated using a lift-off technique.
The electrical measurements are performed in a standard continuous flow cryostat.
The current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the devices are obtained using a 'differential conductance mode' of DC Keithley 2182A/6221 tandem (nanovoltmeter/current source).
The (Ga,Mn)N layer is grown on a reduced threading dislocation density templated sapphire.
The Mn concentration in the (Ga,Mn)N layer is about 5%.
The Si concentration in the n-type GaN buffer layer is 3 × 10^18 cm^-3.
